newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 17.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- Iranian vets demanded that animals from more than twelve Irish counties be excluded in any new beef deal with Ireland.
- The controversial light rail urban transport system for Dublin city got a major boost when the EU lifted its block on 112 million Irish pounds of grant aid to extend the system.
- Irish health minister Michael Noonan apologised to deceased Hepatitis C victim Brigid McCole for insensitive remarks he made in the Irish parliament on Wednesday.
- Multinationals are creating 1,000 jobs each month in new investments in Ireland in 1996, Irish job cretion agency IDA said on Wednesday.

- Eircell, the telecommunications arm of Irish telephone services company Telecom Eireann, said customers must make at least 12 months' rental payments on its new mobile phones, whether they use the service or not.
- An all-out ban on Irish beef sales to Russia would have been a more dangerous scenario than the selective, short term agreement reached at the weekend, Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates said.

- A permanent IRA guerilla ceasefire in Northern Ireland and adherence to the Mitchell principles may not be sufficient to guarantee Sinn Fein's entry into all-party talks, the Irish prime minister John Bruton said.
- The Irish pound fell further against sterling and analysts believe that the British currency is set to rise further.

- The Irish Farmers Association launched a fierce attack on Irish agribusiness firm Waterford Foods on Wednesday night after it cut its milk price and said the move was a bid to "court stockbrokers and institutional shareholders".
- UK-based oil and gas exploration company Premier Oil begins trading on the Irish Stock Exchange on Thursday.

- Irish telecommunications company Telecom Eireann may be forced to sell off its Cabelink arm as new competition enters the Dubln residential cable market, Denis O'Brien, chairman of rival firm Esat Telecom, said.
